proposed_comments.title: Ship a self-consistent Command Palette extension template
proposed_comments.body:
### Ship a self-consistent Command Palette extension template

**Severity:** `high`

Changing only the nested `PackageVersion` does not make generated extensions consume Windows App SDK 2.3.1: the project receives the SDK transitively and the shipped create-extension flow extracts a committed `template.zip`. Add a direct `Microsoft.WindowsAppSDK` package reference, update `Microsoft.Windows.SDK.BuildTools.MSIX` to the minimum required by App SDK 2.3.1, update the publishing guide to depend on `Microsoft.WindowsAppRuntime.2` version 2.3.1, and regenerate the committed archive. Without these changes, newly generated extensions can restore the wrong SDK/runtime or fail to activate on a clean machine.

test_instructions: Open Command Palette, use the create-extension flow, and generate a new extension from the shipped template.
Restore and build the generated x64 Debug extension; verify it resolves Microsoft.WindowsAppSDK 2.3.1 without a package-downgrade warning.
Inspect the generated publishing guide and verify it declares Microsoft.WindowsAppRuntime.2 with MinimumVersion 2.3.1.
Launch the generated extension through Command Palette and verify it activates on a machine with the 2.3 runtime installed.
